name: Spencer Cox
role: Governor of Utah since 2021; lieutenant governor (2013–2021)
summary: Cox combines conservative family and abortion positions with school choice, tax relief and energy expansion. He advocates constitutional restraints on executive power, a less confrontational political culture and selective protections for vulnerable groups, while supporting targeted immigration enforcement and restrictions on some transgender-related policies.

regulate-corporations.rationale: He champions binding social-media safeguards for children, saying companies would not act without strong intervention.

strong-leader.rationale: His defense of judicial independence does not directly address leaders bypassing political gridlock.

limit-guns.rationale: In his candidate questionnaire he explicitly promises to sign permitless concealed-carry legislation.

decide-locally.rationale: He argued for returning education to states and local communities, and for Utah to manage its federal public lands, and said states must be able to act on AI; he did not state a general rule, so only medium.

traditional-family.rationale: His 2025 address calls families foundational and centers marriage, parents and children in public policy.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: On the Obergefell anniversary he said he has a different personal view of marriage, but that from a legal standpoint the protection of couples' rights is really important and he is grateful for it.

abortion-legal.rationale: He identifies his administration as pro-life and explicitly endorses Dobbs returning abortion restrictions to state lawmakers.

more-religion-public.rationale: As governor he repeatedly asked Utahns to unite in prayer for rain and said that, as a man of faith, he makes no excuses for it.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: He urges continuing Utah’s pioneer traditions and proven civic values while welcoming lawful newcomers.

gradual-change.rationale: He invokes inherited constitutional wisdom and warns against dismantling judicial independence for immediate political satisfaction.

reduce-immigration.rationale: He is leading governors to ask for state-issued migrant work permits and a fix of the legal immigration system, which runs against cutting immigration levels, while backing deportation of criminals.

free-trade.rationale: He said he truly believes in free trade as good for all of us and would remove trade barriers everywhere if it were up to him.

open-borders.rationale: He personally directs state agencies to cooperate in identifying and deporting unauthorized immigrants who commit crimes.

limit-growth.rationale: He rejects resource-scarcity pessimism as a reason to stop Utah’s growth, advocating construction and infrastructure instead.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: He said anyone who thinks the country will regulate its way out of climate change is fooling themselves, and that innovation, not cuts in production, is the answer.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: He said that in every past crisis the country has innovated its way out, and holds technology rather than regulation as the route on climate; he does not claim it solves most problems, so only medium.

expand-nuclear.rationale: He explicitly proposes advanced nuclear reactors through Operation Gigawatt.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: He called himself not a big tariffs guy, said tariffs discourage investment and raise consumer prices, and that his economics training says tariffs are bad, while hoping Trump is right and accepting smart, limited barriers.

state-directs-investment.rationale: His proposed FY2026 budget dedicates public investment to nuclear and geothermal energy development.

democracy-best.rationale: He praises constitutional self-government but does not address democracy when voters choose badly.

political-violence-never.rationale: After Kirk's killing he rejected answering violence with violence (asking who he is supposed to shoot now) and said violence is violence; he does not state a general never-justified rule.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Religious language in civic speeches does not establish that legislation should be based on scripture.

limit-population.rationale: He said the experts who warned of overpopulation now correctly cite a falling birth rate as a major risk to civilization, and he praised Utah's high marriage and birth rates.

school-vouchers.rationale: He expressly endorses publicly funded parental education options while insisting that public schools also receive adequate funding.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: He called federal spending of borrowed money reckless, said the 40 trillion dollar national debt looks unsustainable, and linked COVID-era handouts to the inflation spike.

rule-by-example.rationale: He stresses leaders’ moral character without clearly preferring moral example over laws and punishments.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: He defended new federal oil and gas leasing, said cutting domestic production only moves it to Russia and Saudi Arabia, and said coal can keep burning with carbon capture; he pairs this with wind, solar and nuclear.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: He endorses the Declaration’s equal creation and inalienable rights as enduring principles of self-government.

separated-powers.rationale: His SB296 veto defends three independent branches checking one another.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: He explicitly states that Utah is stronger because of its diversity.

death-penalty.rationale: He supports execution in exceptional murder cases, while stressing government fallibility and extremely rare use.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: He promises to execute laws he opposes if the legislature constitutionally overrides his veto.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: He rejects politicizing independent judges, even while supporting constitutional amendment as a lawful remedy.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: He defends restructuring DEI, particularly hiring practices, toward support regardless of background.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: His criticism concerns compulsive consumption and addictive services rather than specifically accumulating possessions and status goods.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: His record combines support for transgender inclusion with restrictions on youth treatment and some sex-based access rules; the reviewed statements do not settle general legal gender recognition.

online-anonymity.rationale: His child-safety age-verification measures do not establish his position on general adult anonymous online participation.

spiritual-nature.rationale: He explicitly endorses spiritual and moral purposes above mere material prosperity as foundations for public life.

collective-bargaining.rationale: His latest position supports repealing a public-sector bargaining ban; this does not establish a preference for collective bargaining over individual contracts generally.

voter-id.rationale: He signed a law moving mail ballots to ID-number verification and praised it, but said voting security must never make it harder for legal voters and that fraud claims are wrong, so his stance on proof of citizenship and ID is mixed.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: He opposed raising Utah's tax on food and services and proposed a large grocery tax credit to ease inflation for families.

notes:
Full 2025 and 2026 state addresses and the judicial-retention veto were downloaded and reviewed. Personal explanations, campaign answers and initiatives drive the audit; signing every legislative bill is not treated as endorsement of every provision. For collective bargaining, his December 2025 explicit support for repeal supersedes the earlier ban. The 2022 sports veto is not generalized into support for all gender-identity policies; later restrictions do not establish his view on every adult recognition question. No views are inferred from church affiliation or party membership. All 490 statements were reviewed. The 2026 general-session veto letter carries an apparent 2025 header despite referring to the 2026 session; it is not used to infer support for a precious-metal payment system he allowed without signature.

Merged with an independent claude-sonnet-5-5 audit: 14 answers taken from it, 6 agreed, 0 conflicts settled by the integrator.

claude-sonnet-5-5 notes: Independent second pass (claude-sonnet-5-5) on top of an earlier audit by another model; sources chosen to differ from it. Searched by theme: economy (taxes, trade, tariffs, unions, welfare, wages, health), government (courts, elections, direct democracy, executive power, federalism, public lands), world (Ukraine, NATO, Israel, Iran, immigration, trade), liberty (guns, surveillance, speech, drugs, political violence), society (abortion, marriage, transgender policy, religion, family), ecology and energy, technology and AI. Six State of the State addresses (2021-2026), the HB11 veto letter, his 2020 written answers, two long interviews (Face the Nation 2026, 60 Minutes 2025) and monthly-news-conference quotes were read. Most themes stay null: his own words on welfare, health care, wages, courts, the military and foreign policy beyond Ukraine support were not found. Not used: the Lieutenant Governor-era votes (no public roll calls), his December 2025 support for repealing the public-union law (only his social-media post reported), the Utah Supreme Court expansion he signed and the Prop 4 repeal push (reports of acts, not his own words on the statements), the March 2026 ICE-facility remarks and National Guard remarks (do not settle a statement). Mixed items are 0 at low. Silence is null.
